notes: DCA initial obligation: 220 units. Borough argued 171 (down from 220). Program Recommendation (Judge Julio Mendez, retired) issued April 17 2025 set prospective need at 190. VLA reduces RDP to 4 units for Fourth Round; 25% of adjusted need adds 1 unit (per statute), bringing effective fourth-round obligation to approximately 5 units. HEFSP approved by Joint Planning Board June 24 2025; endorsed by Borough Council June 25 2025. Developer objections expected July 1 - August 31 2025 window. By March 15 2026 all ordinances must be adopted. Rehabilitation obligation: 0. NJ Builders Association filed objection during 30-day challenge window. The HEFSP filed with Superior Court. Key sites: 137 Patterson Street / The Piermont (256 units / 20 affordable, completed April 2026) for Patterson Street Urban Renewal; a Bergen County United Way group home (4-bedroom very-low income, deed-restricted 40 years); and a 18-townhome project at 100-101 West Street (4 affordable stacked flats). Library.njcourts.gov Bergen documents page does not show a Hillsdale-specific filed HEFSP URL in search snippets; main document is on Hillsdale municipal website.

notes: DCA prospective need: 218 (with 1,000/20% cap). Ho-Ho-Kus had median household income top-coded at $250,000 by Census Bureau affecting calculations. HEFSP adopted by Planning Board and Council by end of June 2025 (exact date not confirmed in snippets; referenced as adopted ahead of June 30 2025 court deadline). Court appearance December 5 2025: Special Adjudicator and Special Master mandated settlement by March 15 2026 or borough loses builder's remedy immunity for 10 years. A developer purchased 1.5-acre parcel on Franklin Turnpike and challenged the HEFSP. Three ordinances adopted Feb/March 2026 as result of court-ordered mediation: (1) new R-6 Planned Residential Townhouse Zone on Franklin Turnpike between cemetery and Blauvelt Avenue; (2) expansion of Downtown Inclusionary Overlay Zone (OL-1 through OL-4); (3) updated development fees ordinance. Borough has existing Settlement Agreement with FSHC (prior rounds) requiring Very Low-Income Monitoring Reports. 619 North (619 N Maple Ave) is existing development with 10 affordable units. No library.njcourts.gov HEFSP URL found for Ho-Ho-Kus in search results; HEFSP page is on municipal website. Settlement date for Fourth Round not confirmed.

notes: DCA Fourth Round: present need 68 units (rehabilitation), prospective need 104 units (1,000/20% cap also 104). Borough adopted Fourth Round obligation via Resolution 2025-78 on January 22 2025. Third and Fourth Round HEFSP adopted June 26 2025 (amended version filed with court). NJ Judge granted Leonia temporary zoning immunity; borough still needs formal Judgment of Compliance. Developer High Jump Realty challenged HEFSP claiming borough cannot meet obligation without approving high-density proposal - borough disputes this, stating Redevelopment Plan covers all four rounds and much of Round 5. Ordinance 2025-22 (adopted Oct 20 2025) adopts Redevelopment Plan for Blocks 802 (Lots 12-19), 803 (Lots 35-37), 1202 (Lots 2-5), 1203, 1204, 503, and others along Fort Lee Road and Willow Tree Road corridors. Affordable housing set-aside for inclusionary projects: 20%. Rental units under affordability controls subject to 40-year deed restriction. January 2025 resolution document available on Leonia's cloud server. Expert Report filed with NJ Courts January 22 2025.
